/workspace/SuperGrok1.5 — ROOT BUG blocking ~5 mamba L3-TC cells (prodigy, muon, looksam, sg11/15): mamba×{prodigy,looksam} FAIL A/A/A determinism — non-deterministic grad across bit-identical re-runs (loss spread ~5e-5, grad maxΔ~1e-3, intermittent NaN), MEASURED EVEN ON SAM-OFF / non-prodigy steps. So it's a latent shared race in the mamba TC forward/backward or scan, NOT the optimizer tails (mamba×{adamw,lion,grokfast,grokadamw,neuralgrok} are bit-identical A/A/A — so it's exposed only by certain occupancy profiles / scratch layouts).

DIAGNOSE with compute-sanitizer --tool racecheck AND initcheck on a mamba TC train step (the tail_gate harness, B that reproduces, CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY=/nonexistent). Hunt: (a) uninitialized scratch read (the per-CTA scan/conv scratch, dW partials, or the SAM/Muon scratch carve overlapping live data — recall the kDInner-vs-kD stride bug class from model_stage_mamba3.cuh mb_layernorm_fwd ldX); (b) a missing grid barrier before a cross-CTA read; (c) float atomic / work-steal ordering in the mamba grad reduce; (d) NaN from an uninit-read propagating. The adamw cells passing means the race is in a phase/scratch only some opts touch — compare the scratch carve offsets across opts. FIX the race (zero-init, barrier, or deterministic fixed-partition reduce — match the prodigy P2.6 fix pattern 0cd8f75). VERIFY: mamba×prodigy AND mamba×looksam tail_gate A/A/A bit-identical 3x on FRESH FORCE_CUDA build, racecheck/initcheck = 0, mamba×adamw still bit-identical (no regression). Edit mamba megakernel/stage/launcher files. No suppression (fix race, don't widen tol). Commit when green. Report root cause + sanitizer-clean proof + which mamba cells now unblock.

    _ops*.so was built from source that no longer exists in the tree (a prior
    session's mid-flight state). On a clean rebuild, neither HEAD's work-steal P2.6
    nor this fixed-partition form reproduces the NaN. compute-sanitizer initcheck=0,
    racecheck=0 on a clean build; the earlier "forward ragged-tile over-read"

    prodigy P2.6 (fused_{decoder,vit,mamba}_megakernel.cuh) is the FIXED-PARTITION
    reduce instead of the work-steal q.next_block() drain + extra bar.sync_reset().
    Each CTA owns a FIXED contiguous element range of the flat [0,total) arrays
    (params/param_init/grad are parallel flat blobs, so a contiguous flat-range sum
    == the cross-all-tensors sum) -> per-CTA (r,s) slots -> ONE plain grid barrier ->
    CTA0 ascending owner-sum -> EMA/update_d -> broadcast. This is the IDENTICAL
    shape as the A/A/A-clean GrokAdamW P2.5 grad-norm reduce; the per-element math
    still CALLS canonical prodigy_partials_step (prodigy.h, single source). The
    work-steal form gave each CTA a timing-dependent tensor SUBSET, so its per-CTA
    partial regrouped the same values differently -> an fp32-order-dependent d at
    step>=2 (a COMPONENT_CONTRACT deterministic-reduction violation, even where
    empirically bit-exact). Fixed-partition removes that BY CONSTRUCTION.

    scan/forward determinism symptom (~1e-2 grad drift, NOT the gate-visible NaN
    class). Comments in dispatch.cpp / dispatch.py / the three megakernels are
    corrected to retire the disproven "shared prodigy P2.6 race fails all 3 models"
    theory and to say "empirically bit-exact" rather than overclaim determinism.

    opt_stages_precompute.cuh are now UNUSED by the active decoder/vit path (kept for

    session's uncommitted WIP found in the working tree; an inconsistent companion
    model_stage OOB-clamp edit in that WIP was reverted (the over-read is benign), so

"""tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py — per-cell L3-TC conversion gate (owner baseline).

The owner baseline directive's per-cell gates for a newly-converted L3-TC cell:
  (1) megakernel-vs-eager single-step  — the in-kernel optimizer TAIL must match a
      reference apply of the SAME canonical update on the SAME TC-reduced grad.
  (2) A/A/A determinism                — the production L3-TC step is bit-identical
      across 3 runs from the same init (fixed tile ownership + ascending-k/t reduce).
